chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Ayoub, brother of Udaym, the seller of al-Harawi, said:

We were sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when al-Ala' ibn Kamal approached and sat in front of him. He said, 'Pray to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He grants me sustenance in a leisurely manner (without excessive effort).' He replied, 'I will not pray for you; seek (sustenance) as Allah has commanded you.'

key_terms.اَلْعَلاَءُ بْنُ كَامِلٍ: Ala' ibn Kamal, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.اُطْلُبْ: Seek (imperative), referring to striving for livelihood

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between praying for easy sustenance and actively seeking it according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on trade (al-Makasib) illustrates the Shia principle that divine supplication complements, rather than replaces, human effort (asbab). Imam al-Sadiq’s rejection of a passive request for 'easy' sustenance underscores the theological balance between tawakkul (trust in God) and taking practical means, a key concept in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the conditions of valid dua.
